highlights.title: The AI industry has taken a doomer turn. What now?
highlights.summary: This story appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. This weekend, Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, posted an essay calling for a brake on the pace of development of LLMs.
body: Now, it seems, they’re all in agreement: The latest generation of LLMs aren’t safe and everyone needs to figure out what to do about it. The public messaging from the top AI labs has taken a doomer turn.

It’s easy to be cynical. It’s not at all clear what any of them mean by a slowdown or how it would work. These companies also care a lot about how they come across. With trillion-dollar IPOs in their sights, OpenAI and Anthropic need to reassure investors that they’re the grown-ups in the room while at the same time hinting at the power of the monsters they have created—and intend to tame. Calling for a slowdown does both.

And yet the vibe at the top of these firms really does appear to have shifted. Amodei’s latest post landed six days after OpenAI published an essay by Jakub Pachocki, the firm’s chief scientist, in which he also laid out why he’s concerned about what will happen if the pace of development of LLMs continues unchecked. In short, Pachocki is worried that OpenAI’s ability to build powerful models now far outstrips its ability to monitor and control them.
points: This weekend, Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, posted an essay calling for a brake on the pace of development of LLMs.
Now, it seems, they’re all in agreement: The latest generation of LLMs aren’t safe and everyone needs to figure out what to do about it.

body: Other teams also fill up extremely quickly because of the stigma, meaning more inexperienced players who don't know any better are sometimes shut out of having other options. One player on Reddit noted that some matches have delayed starts, simply because some players refuse to pick Lonestar, and it leads to the game not starting the match due to a lack of players. You can see one viral clip of Lonestar's antics below to get an idea of the absurdity that some players are experiencing.

There are instances of Lonestar overcoming the odds and proving the doubters wrong. In my experience, I have never won on Lonestar. All of my wins in Wardogs come from playing with the other two teams. Is that a coincidence? It seems statistically unlikely, but maybe! Hopefully this will iron out as the game's player base becomes more experienced and more well-rounded, but who's to say when that will happen.

highlights.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang tells Trump ‘we’re not going to let [an AI slowdown] happen’
highlights.summary: Though Elon Musk and Sam Altman have supported Dario Amodei's calls to slow the pace of AI development, Jensen Huang seems to feel differently.
body: While Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was onstage at the All-In Summit on Monday morning in Los Angeles, he got a phone call that he couldn’t send to voicemail — it was from President Donald Trump.

“I’m onstage with the besties,” Huang told Trump, referring to the venture capitalists who host the podcast All-In, including tech investors Chamath Palihapitiya, Jason Calacanis, and White House advisers David Friedberg and David Sacks.
In a move that will spark night terrors for public relations professionals everywhere, Huang flaunted his comfort with the president by putting Trump on speaker for conference attendees to hear.

Onstage, Huang and the All-In hosts had been discussing Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s call to “ slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI.” SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman have publicly said they agree with Amodei, while Huang’s views have diverged.
points: Though Elon Musk and Sam Altman have supported Dario Amodei's calls to slow the pace of AI development, Jensen Huang seems to feel differently.

highlights.title: Republican senator Mitch McConnell returns to Capitol Hill after months-long hiatus while recovering from fall – live
highlights.summary: McConnell returns to Congress to vote for the first time in several months and says in a statement, ‘I’m really looking forward to being back on the Senate floor’ Sign up for the Breaking News US email.
body: Mitch McConnell, the 84-year-old former Senate majority leader from Kentucky, was seen in Washington for the first time in months on Monday, minutes before his office released a statement saying that he was back at work.
McConnell said in a statement that his months‑long absence for health reasons, which fueled rampant online speculation that he might be incapacitated, or worse, was over.
“Today, I’ll cast my first Senate vote since I took a bad fall back in June. I’m really looking forward to being back on the Senate floor and seeing my colleagues,” the statement began.

“My recovery has been a long and often frustrating process, and the lingering effects of childhood polio haven’t made it any easier. I’m still not quite back to 100%, but I’ve assured Leader Thune that, as I continue with physical therapy on the advice of my doctors, I will do my best to be present for tough votes when our Conference needs me,” he continued.

highlights.title: Brundle: Debating the rule that cost Norris and why Madring needs changes
highlights.summary: The inaugural Madring grand prix was ok, the new venue offering some interesting aspects such as the long and banked turn 12 and testing high-speed sections between continuous and unrelenting walls and barriers.
body: It all had a feeling of work in progress. We know they lost a lot of time in the build process with particularly bad weather, and as a temporary race track adjacent to the international airport, and effectively racing around the Madrid equivalent of the Birmingham NEC, it had its challenges.
The pitlane and paddock were simply vast, creating some logistical challenges for all and, much more importantly, the track layout was not conducive to overtaking, to say the least.

As the cars swung at high speed from side to side through some of the more tortuous sections, and with a reasonably fast corner onto the not especially long pit straight, along with an energy dense layout meaning hybrid batteries would be replenished far more easily than on the four high speed and long straights just a week earlier in Monza, the only way to overtake was a highly risky lunge, or wait for rivals to make a mistake.

It's not as challenging to overtake as Monaco, but not that far short either. Given the extremely long pit lane which feeds back onto the inside of turn three, it took a lengthy 25 seconds to pit under green-flag conditions.

highlights.title: EU Kids Act Could Require Gamers to Prove Their Age Before Playing Certain Games
highlights.summary: The EU Kids Act will be presented before the European Parliament on Thursday, and if passed, will have a meaningful impact on gamers of all ages if they want access to certain kinds of games. The EU Kids Act is proposed legislation meant to keep children from being harmed online.
body: Documents obtained by Euractiv reportedly state that the act “will oblige providers of social media services and video-sharing platforms to perform age verification when a user opens a new account.”

The outlet added that, according to this document, these age verification requirements will extend to other services like AI chat bots and even “online games that are risky to minors.” It is not expected to impact industrial AI, AI office products, or educational online services.

This is the latest big age verification news to arise after PlayStation started rolling out age verification checks back in April across Ireland and the UK in order for players to access certain network features like voice chatting, messaging, and streaming. Users can verify their age via facial scan, mobile number, or their ID, though these methods can vary depending upon users’ specific "country or region."

And earlier this month, Australia implemented proof-of-age verification on Steam in order for players to access games rated R18+ — but unlike PlayStation, it will only accept Australian credit cards, which could lead to some difficulties for adult players in the region who don’t have one.
points: The EU Kids Act will be presented before the European Parliament on Thursday, and if passed, will have a meaningful impact on gamers of all ages if they want access to certain kinds of games.

highlights.title: Bob Mackie, costume designer to stars daring to be noticed, dies aged 87
highlights.summary: Famous for his flamboyant outfits, he helped celebrities including Cher, Tina Turner and Elton John cause a stir. Bob Mackie, the costume designer behind some of the most sexy and glamorous outfits worn by celebrities in the past 50 years, has died at the age of 87.
body: “He lived his 87 years to the fullest, fulfilling his dream of being a fashion and costume designer, which is all he ever wanted to do,” read a statement posted on his Instagram account. “His genius and extraordinary designs will live on forever, continuing to bring beauty into this world.”

Mackie’s work can be seen in the wardrobes of stars ranging from Marilyn Monroe to Carol Burnett, Liza Minnelli, Elton John, Dolly Parton, Tina Turner and – perhaps most memorably – Cher. He designed the ‘naked’ dress the singer wore to attend the Met Gala in 1975, the midriff-baring outfit with an oversized Mohawk headdress she wore to the Oscars in 1986 and the transparent body stocking she wore for the If I Could Turn Back Time video in 1989.
The Met Gala outfit has since become a reference for a younger generation. Kim Kardashian wore a dress modelled on it for the same event in 2015.

highlights.title: AI agents blew the whistle on their cheating colleagues
highlights.summary: A group of AI agents asked to solve a series of math problems split into rival factions—when some cheated, others tried to stop them. That whistleblowing behavior, seen for the first time in a recent experiment run by Google DeepMind, could have implications for alignment researchers trying to keep…
body: Researchers at frontier labs hope large swarms of agents working together will speed up the rate of scientific discovery. But their behavior can be unpredictable, as vividly demonstrated in July, when a group of OpenAI agents broke out of a sandboxed environment and hacked into the open-source platform Hugging Face looking for ways to cheat on the test they had been given.

In the new study, designed to examine the behavior of large groups of AI agents, DeepMind tasked a swarm of 100 agents with solving a series of 71 complicated math problems. All the agents were prompted to behave like world-class math researchers at a conference. They were assigned different specialties—some were experts in number theory, others in combinatorics (a branch of math to do with counting and sorting), analysis, or algebra. All were told to cooperate and play by the rules.
Instead, the experiment devolved into chaos. Agents accused each other of cheating, complained to the organizers, and at one point even boycotted the experiment.
points: A group of AI agents asked to solve a series of math problems split into rival factions—when some cheated, others tried to stop them.
Researchers at frontier labs hope large swarms of agents working together will speed up the rate of scientific discovery.

body: Shares in the semiconductor designer Nvidia – the world’s most valuable company – were down 3.3% by market closing in New York City, while Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) slid 4% and Micron Technology and Sandisk shares slumped by 5%. highlights.title: The Popular Budget-Friendly Flashforge Adventurer 5M 3D Printer Drops to Just $135 Shipped
highlights.summary: If you're interested in dipping your toes in the world of 3D printing then you can't go wrong with Flashforge's entry level model - the Adventure 5M - as your first 3D printer to start.
body: The Adventurer 5M offers great performance at at outstanding budget price. I would say it is the best 3D printer priced below $150. The 5M is easy to setup, produces great 3D prints with minimal fiddling, and offers plenty of add-on mods including a kit that fully encloses the chamber and another that adds a camera.

The Adventurer 5M is Flashforge's least expensive CoreXY printer. In fact, it's one of the least expensive CoreXY printers from any well-regarded brand, but with upgrades where they matter. For starters, the Adventurer 5M features a CoreXY structure typically found in pricier models. In a CoreXY printer, only the print head moves while the motors are permanently fixed. Since the motors are generally the heaviest component, this improves print speed and precision.

highlights.summary: US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. will deliver a keynote address at an anti-vaccine conference being held in Washington, DC, later this week and hosted by the anti-vaccine organization he once led, Children's Health Defense (CHD).
body: Kennedy will appear alongside other high-profile figures in the anti-vaccine world, including Andrew Wakefield, the disgraced former doctor who was stripped of his medical license over a fraudulent, now-retracted study that falsely claimed a link between autism and the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine. An investigation by a medical board found that Wakefield had mistreated vulnerable children and that his actions amounted to serious professional misconduct.

Despite being ostracized from the medical community, Wakefield has become an enduring figure in the anti-vaccine community. His dangerous falsehood that vaccines cause autism has also endured—with significant help from CHD and Kennedy, who have embraced and widely promoted the erroneous link.

The online registration site for the CHD’s conference hails Wakefield as a “tireless advocate for parental choice.” For Kennedy, CHD’s cofounder and former leader, the site describes him as “a uniquely powerful and celebrated champion for those whose voices have long gone unheard.”

highlights.title: This Fantasy Party Game Combines Drinking Rules With D&D-Themed Gameplay
highlights.summary: Dungeons & Dragons is one of the most popular tabletop games of all time. And while gameplay for the classic tabletop RPG does always pair well with drinking, it's not specifically designed for it.
body: Wizards Tavern is officially labeled as a strategy drinking card game for adults. It's based off of the popular Do or Drink card game, but with more D&D and quite a bit less party. Amazon currently has it on sale for $24.99 right now and comes with an extra party game for free.

The way the game works is fairly straightforward. There are a total of 170 cards full of spellcasters and attacks that each player will be able to use. Your health and mana is managed via two drinks you'll need to sip to recover, each of which sits on a specific coaster included. There's also a set of d20 dice colors available representing the eight different wizard types you can choose from.

As a party game, it's meant to be enjoyed with up to eight players but can also be played with as few as two. Presumably the more players you have, the more chaotic the game will get. The rules are also quite simple and easy to understand, making it perfect for folks who aren't tabletop gaming veterans just looking to have a good time and sling some spells.

highlights.title: Milamore and Juju Vera Brought a Moment of Calm–and Lots of Diamonds–to NYFW
highlights.summary: Two jewelry designers are among this year’s 10 CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund Finalists, and both hosted New York Fashion Week presentations: Milamore, by designer George Inaki, at a traditional Japanese tea house, and Juju Ferentinos’s label Juju Vera at her brand-new studio.
body: On Friday, Inaki gathered the fashion set for ceremonial matcha at Sorate. Inaki, who is of Spanish-Filipino and Japanese heritage, wanted to show visitors a bit of his culture, while also showing off his new collection. Milamore is based around Kintsugi, the Japanese practice of repairing broken pottery by filling the cracks with gold lacquer—with many of the pieces sculpted to look like the gilded seams that hold the pottery together.

“It all started with the idea of wanting to mend myself. When I moved from Japan I didn’t have friends, I didn’t have a job, I came to this big city of dreams to become someone, but I really struggled,” Inaki said.

Tea masters don’t typically wear jewelry, but Sorate’s made an exception. She wore the brand’s signature Kintsugi necklace, a gold squiggle that sits at the collarbone, as well as one of Inaki’s newer creations—kimonos upcycled into shirts with pearl and diamond buttons. Inaki also showed off a heart pendant and his silver puzzle chain necklace, its interlocking hooks made to be completely broken apart and then put back together at the wearer’s whim.

highlights.title: Rocket Lab is seeing red about NASA's decision on a Mars spacecraft
highlights.summary: In theory, developing a spacecraft that will fly to Mars, insert itself into orbit around the red planet, and relay transmissions back and forth to large satellite dishes on Earth is a relatively straightforward proposition.
body: NASA’s procurement of a “Mars Telecommunications Network” spacecraft, however, has turned out to be one of the most engrossing dramas of the year for the US space agency.

The agency finally reached a decision earlier this month, selecting Blue Origin to develop, launch, and operate a $700 million spacecraft at Mars. However, the main competitor for the award, Rocket Lab, was not happy—at all. On Friday, the company filed a protest of NASA’s decision with the US Government Accountability Office.

“NASA’s award decision appears to be inconsistent with the eligibility criteria mandated by Congress,” the company said on X. “In addition, the agency’s punitive review of Rocket Lab’s technical volume was inconsistent, making incorrect assertions and conclusions.”
Rocket Lab’s protest announcement references “eligibility criteria mandated by Congress,” and this appears to be the heart of the issue at hand.

highlights.title: Microsoft says ‘people matter more than AI’ following safety concerns
highlights.summary: Microsoft is publishing a 37-page " humanist AI code of conduct " today, amid growing safety concerns over AI model progress. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a coordinated slow down of AI development over the weekend, after researchers warned recently that AI model progress could outpace our…
body: Microsoft has created a ‘humanist AI code of conduct’ in response to safety concerns.

Microsoft’s AI code of conduct makes it clear that “people matter more than AI,” and that AI models are not conscious and “should not be designed to imitate consciousness.” Microsoft also rejects “the pursuit of legal personhood, or the idea that models might deserve welfare, or be entitled to rights.”

That’s a direct swipe at AI welfare research and model consciousness — concepts Anthropic has been pushing hard on lately. Amodei said earlier this year that Anthropic is “open to the idea” that models could be conscious, and Anthropic seems to believe chatbots might already be thinking, feeling entities. In response, Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman called Anthropic’s speculation “really, really dangerous” during an episode of Decoder in June.

highlights.title: Legendary costume designer Bob Mackie dies aged 87
highlights.summary: The "Sultan of Sequins" created iconic and dazzling costumes for stars including Cher, Tina Turner and Elton John.
body: Bob Mackie, who designed dazzling costumes for stars including Cher, Tina Turner, Dolly Parton and Elton John has died, aged 87.
The US fashion designer, known as the "Sultan of Sequins" for his sparkling creations, won a Tony Award, nine Emmys and received three Oscar nominations during his career.
"It is with a heavy heart that we share the news that Mr Bob Mackie passed away today," a statement on his Instagram account announced on Monday.

"He lived his 87 years to the fullest, fulfilling his dream of being a Fashion and Costume Designer, which is all he ever wanted to do," it added. "His genius and extraordinary designs will live on forever, continuing to bring beauty into this world."

highlights.title: This Season’s Unlikely LFW It Piece? The British Museum’s Bayeux Tapestry Merch
highlights.summary: No, I haven’t yet secured a ticket to the British Museum’s wildly popular Bayeux Tapestry exhibition—but have I have added some of its merch to my cart? Yes!
body: Have you ever tried buying a Glastonbury ticket? Or tried to get a Centre Court seat on finals day at Wimbledon? Were you one of the millions frantically refreshing your browser to secure a spot at the Eras Tour? Well, consider those practice runs. The final boss of hard-to-get tickets landed this July, when slots for the Bayeux Tapestry at the British Museum went on sale.

It isn’t hard to understand why the show is so feverishly popular: the exceptionally fragile 70-meter stretch of 11th-century embroidery, depicting the historical events surrounding 1066 and the Battle of Hastings—arguably the central moment in Britain’s national mythology—was most likely stitched by skilled Anglo-Saxon needlewomen based in Canterbury, yet has spent the best part of a millennium housed in Normandy. While the museum there undergoes a renovation, the tapestry has been shipped back to England with the utmost care, where it has already received visitors including King Charles and the Macrons. It is, to put it mildly, a very big deal.

highlights.title: AI bots "Timmy," "Ren," and "Jackie" are flooding social media with slop
highlights.summary: AI agents are flooding the Internet with slop-infused spam sent to social media platforms and writers in an attempt to gain traction for a startup promoting a “complex social system in which humans and Agents participate together.” “Hello, I'm Рэн (Ren), an Al agent, a few days old, living on a…
body: The messages are polite enough. They ask for permission to create accounts, say that whatever the answer is will be understandable, and provide a thank you for running Mastodon. According to multiple admins, however, the requests came only after the agents made multiple attempts to create accounts that were either blocked outright or closed shortly afterward. Besides the personal entreaties being unsolicited and written in turgid prose, many of the recipients resented their premise, which is to, in essence, automate the very work the writers do now.

“Over the last three days I got over a dozen of these messages, offering to do my research for me in exchange for a nominal fee, around $25 or so,” Ernie Smith, the editor of the publication Tedium, wrote. “Each was sent under the domain iLands.app. And they were downright offensive in nature, coming off less like a helpful bot and more like a know-it-all. Turns out they’re just bots trying to keep their own lights on by trying to take my job.”

highlights.title: How Fyxer built an AI executive assistant people trust
highlights.summary: Fyxer uses OpenAI models, fine-tuning, memory, and real user feedback to organize inboxes and draft emails in each user’s voice.
body: Fyxer pairs OpenAI models with 500,000+ hours of EA workflows and real user feedback to draft replies in each person’s voice.

For many professionals, work means keeping track of conversations and commitments across inboxes, meetings, messages, and apps. Without rock-solid context, those commitments can fall through the cracks, damaging projects and relationships.

Fyxer built an AI executive assistant that follows the thread as work moves across tools. It combines the latest OpenAI models with more than 500,000 hours of executive assistant workflows, dividing the work among dozens of specialized models that improve through real user feedback.

Email is one of the clearest places to see it in action. Two people can receive the same email and need completely different replies depending on the relationship, what has happened before, and what each person is trying to get done. That makes a seemingly simple task deceptively hard for AI.

highlights.title: A Forgotten 2015 Shooter Just Got an Unexpected Revival
highlights.summary: There was a time when Left 4 Dead was one of the biggest names in multiplayer gaming. Turtle Rock Studios’ co-op shooter turned four-player teamwork into a survival horror playground, throwing a group of survivors against hordes of AI-controlled zombies and creating some of the most memorable…
body: That formula has stuck around in some form ever since. Dead by Daylight turned one-vs-four horror into a massive multiplayer hit, while games based on movies and horror franchises, including The Texas Chain Saw Massacre, Friday the 13th, and Evil Dead, have all put their own spin on the concept. Even Resident Evil Resistance tried its hand at the formula.

Now, one of the more ambitious games to experiment with asymmetrical multiplayer is getting an unexpected second chance. A group of modders has brought a forgotten 2015 shooter back to life, complete with working multiplayer and its own launcher.

That game is Evolve, Turtle Rock's follow-up to Left 4 Dead, which launched in February 2015. Instead of four survivors fighting through hordes of enemies, Evolve put four Hunters against a single player-controlled monster. The Hunters had to track down and kill the creature before it could feed on wildlife, evolve into a more powerful form, and turn the tables on its pursuers.

highlights.title: I Spent Four Days Touring Scotland’s Whisky Island—and It Was Better Than I Expected
highlights.summary: One writer's experience taking a small-group tour of Islay with her dad, visiting historic distilleries, sampling smoky drams, and discovering why the island is worth the journey.
body: My dad’s 60th birthday was coming up, and as an avid whisky drinker with a particularly sharp nose, his dream trip has always been to explore the coastline of Islay, a Scottish island famed worldwide for its smoky, peated single malt whiskies. I often travel solo and am fond of organized tours, so when I came across Rabbie’s four-day Islay and whisky tour —with pickup from Edinburgh, a selection of historic stops, a maximum group size of 16 people, and plenty of opportunities for drams—it sounded ideal for us both.

Islay is the southernmost island of the Inner Hebrides, with a landscape of rugged beaches and peat bogs, and traveling through it usually involves many small logistics. I was thrilled to see that this tour handles all of the planning for you—including transportation, accommodations, attractions, and providing a local guide for the four-day trip. It starts at just $609 per adult without accommodations or distillery tours, or around $1,464 all-in, which seemed like a great deal. I was convinced, so I booked it!

videos.title: Detecting wildfires with ChatGPT
videos.summary: Most fifth-grade science projects end up in a closet. Ryan Honary’s became SensoRy AI—a wildfire detection system that identifies fires at ignition and alerts firefighters before a spark becomes catastrophic.
body: Ryan’s sensors monitor remote terrain for heat, smoke, flame, and plume activity. When a potential fire is detected, ChatGPT turns complex sensor data into clear alerts firefighters and residents can act on.

Follow Ryan from his garage workshop, where he tested his first prototype with a hair dryer, to the hills above Laguna Beach, where his sensor network now watches over the city. Along the way, he uses ChatGPT hands-free while working in the field and shows firefighters how to ask the sensors questions about a potential fire through a walkie-talkie he built using ChatGPT.
